chunks: Ṣafwān narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Abū ʿAmr al-Bazzāz who said:

We were sitting with Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) when he stood up, entered the house, and came out. He held the two doorposts, greeted us, and we replied to his greeting. Then he said, 'By Allah, I surely love you, and the scent and spirit of your souls. Verily, you are upon the religion of Allah and the religion of His angels. And nothing stands between any of you and seeing that which would gladden his eye except his soul reaching here,' and he pointed to his throat with his hand. And he said, 'Be mindful of Allah and support that with piety.'

key_terms.وَرَعٍ: piety and devotion, specifically cautiousness in avoiding doubtful matters

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the proximity of death and the importance of piety?
ai.summary: Imam Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) physically demonstrates the proximity of death by pointing to his throat, emphasizing that the transition from life to the sight of one's deeds is immediate upon the soul reaching the throat. This narration, recorded in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia emphasis on *waraʿ* (piety/conscientiousness) as the essential safeguard for a good *khatimah* (final end). The act of greeting the doorposts further highlights the intimate, personal nature of the believer's encounter with the divine in the final moments.
